column4: sCureBox - Domain
column5:
h3. Domain — overview

{{SCureBox.Domain}} is the pure business-rule layer of the sCureBox firmware (reference version 1.0.152): a .NET 10 class library with *no I/O apart from {{ErrorRegistry.Load}} reading one file, no framework dependencies and no package references*. It holds the hardware naming model (fans, LED panels, thermistors, UV photoresistors), the central error-code registry ({{ErrorCodes}} + {{config/errors.json}}), the curing-program model (materials and steps with their exact wire/CSV spelling), program validation, the CSV import/export format, the program duration estimator, the recipe sequencer state machine, sensor conversion maths (NTC, chamber calibration, N2 pressure), signal helpers (slope, tachometer RPM, glitch hold), the heater PI + delta-sigma controller, HDT calibration maths, every supervision evaluator that raises a 9xxx alert (open thermistor, frozen reading, heater not heating, fan wear/failure, LED panel not heating / temperature drop, UV light not detected, output watchdog) and the RGB status-strip priority ladder. Every evaluator is a deterministic, single-threaded object: the caller passes {{now}} (a {{DateTimeOffset}} or monotonic seconds) and readings in, and gets verdicts, alert dictionaries ({{code -> detail text}}) or commands out. Config values (components.json) are mapped into the domain {{*Rules}} records by the Hardware / Application layers; the domain itself only reads {{config/errors.json}}. Unit tests live in {{tests/SCureBox.Domain.Tests}} (xUnit) and some of them read {{config/errors.json}}, {{config/presets.json}} and the whole {{src/}} tree.

column4: sCureBox - Hardware
column5:
h2. 03 - Hardware area (SCureBox.Hardware)

h3. Hardware — overview

{{src/SCureBox.Hardware}} (namespace root {{SCureBox.Hardware}}) is the hardware abstraction of the sCure appliance: a Raspberry Pi CM5 on the sCure IO board *BRD-74205 rev07*. It exposes ONE facade, {{IHardwareSystem}}, with two implementations: {{IoBoardHardwareSystem}} (the real board: PCA9685 + TCA6424A + two ADS1115 over Linux I2C, GPIO via libgpiod, damper servo + RGB strip via RP1-PIO helper processes) and {{SimulatedHardwareSystem}} (deterministic model driven by a {{TimeProvider}}). Every write in production goes through {{Safety.FreezableHardwareSystem}} (DVT hang gate). A separate process mode ({{scurebox --watchdog}}, {{Safety.OutputWatchdog}}) cuts heater + UV LEDs when the firmware heartbeat goes stale. The live machine configuration comes from {{components.json}} ({{IHardwareConfig}}, hot-reloaded every 1 s).

Build settings (repo {{Directory.Build.props}}, applies to every project): {{net10.0}}, {{Nullable=enable}}, {{ImplicitUsings=enable}}, {{LangVersion=latest}}, {{TreatWarningsAsErrors=true}} (except CS1591, xUnit1004), {{InvariantGlobalization=true}}, {{NoWarn CA1416}}.

h4. Hardware channel map (IO board BRD-74205 rev07, as used by the code)

*Buses / chips*

||Chip||Board ref||Linux bus||7-bit addr||Used for||Driver class||
| PCA9685 16-ch 12-bit PWM | U15 | {{/dev/i2c-0}} (GPIO0/1, {{dtparam=i2c_vc=on}}) | 0x55 | fans, heater SSR, chamber light, motor enables, BOFA speed ref, UV LED DIM | {{Pca9685}} |
| TCA6424A 24-bit IO expander | U1 | {{/dev/i2c-0}} | 0x23 | LED_SWITCH relay K4, door magnet/valves, motor direction, NFC reset | {{Tca6424a}} |
| ADS1115 16-bit ADC | U6 | {{/dev/i2c-0}} | 0x49 | UV photoresistors, Left/Right panel NTCs (PGA 1, +/-4.096 V) | {{Ads1115}} |
| ADS1115 16-bit ADC | U7 | {{/dev/i2c-1}} (GPIO2/3, {{dtparam=i2c_arm=on}}) | 0x49 | Back/Door/Chamber NTCs + N2 pressure (PGA 1) | {{Ads1115}} |
| ADS1115 | U8 | {{/dev/i2c-0}} | 0x48 | analog sensors - NOT used by the C# code | - |
| ADS1115 | U10 | {{/dev/i2c-1}} | 0x48 | light sensors - NOT used by the C# code | - |

All I2C transactions of the process share ONE global lock ({{SystemDeviceI2cBus.GlobalLock}}).

*PCA9685 channels (0x55)* - logical duty 0..100 %; "inverted" = the board has an inverting driver stage, the code writes 100-duty.

||Ch||Name||Function||Inverted||Notes||
| 0 | FAN_HEATER | heater fan PWM | yes | tach GPIO22 |
| 1 | FAN_DOOR | door LED-panel fan | yes | tach GPIO23 |
| 2 | FAN_RIGHT | right LED-panel fan | yes | tach GPIO24 |
| 3 | FAN_LEFT | left LED-panel fan | yes | tach GPIO19 |
| 4 | FAN_BACK | back LED-panel fan | yes | tach GPIO25 |
| 5 | FAN_COOLING | chamber cooling / intake fan | yes | tach GPIO26 |
| 6 | PWM_HEATER | heater SSR K3 | no | DIGITAL: any duty>0 = full on |
| 7 | LIGHT1 | chamber light | yes | {{SetLight}} writes 100/0 |
| 8 | MOT1_EN | L298N enable 1 | yes | not driven by the facade (safe state 0) |
| 9 | MOT2_EN | L298N enable 2 | yes | not driven by the facade (safe state 0) |
| 10 | BOFA | extraction-fan 0-10 V speed reference (RC-filtered, x3.3 op-amp U18B on 12 V rail) | no | 60 % channel duty = 10 V ({{bofa.max_duty}}) |
| 11 | LED_BACK | UV LED driver DIM | no | 405 nm only |
| 12 | LED_DOOR | UV LED driver DIM | no | 405 + 450 nm |
| 13 | LED_RIGHT | UV LED driver DIM | no | 405 nm only |
| 14 | LED_LEFT | UV LED driver DIM | no | 405 nm only |
| 15 | LED_ANALOG5 | unused | no | safe state 0 |

Register write per channel: 4-byte block at {{0x06 + 4*ch}} = {{[on & 0xFF, on >> 8, off & 0xFF, off >> 8]}}; full-on {{(on=0x1000, off=0)}}, full-off {{(0, 0x1000)}}, partial {{(0, (int)(eff/100*4095))}} (truncation). LED brightness: physical duty = percent * {{led_max_duty}}(60) / 100. BOFA: channel duty = percent * {{bofa.max_duty}}(60) / 100.

*TCA6424A pins (0x23)* - registers with auto-increment bit: INPUT 0x80, OUTPUT 0x84, CONFIG 0x8C (3 bytes each, ports 0..2; CONFIG bit 1 = input).

||Pin||Port.bit||Function||Polarity||
| NFC_RESET | P0.1 | NFC reader reset | active low; safe = HIGH |
| LED_SWITCH | P0.5 | -> Q28 -> relay K4 (selects LED_OUT1/LED_OUT2 at J21) | 1 while 405 nm runs, 0 at rest / 450 nm |
| FAN1_ONOFF..FAN6_ONOFF | P1.1..P1.6 | fan on/off (unused by facade) | inverted (logical 1 = LOW) |
| MOT1_IN1 / MOT1_IN2 | P2.5 / P2.4 | motor 1 direction | - |
| MOT2_IN1 / MOT2_IN2 | P2.2 / P2.1 | motor 2 direction | - |
| VALVE_2_ON = DOOR_MAGNET | P2.6 | valve 2 output = door magnet (J8_DOOR_MAGNET) | active high |
| VALVE_1_ON | P2.7 | valve 1 | active high |

Safe-init bytes: OUTPUT {{[0x02, 0x7E, 0x00]}} written first, then CONFIG {{[0xDD, 0x81, 0x09]}}.

*ADS1115 channels* (single-ended, PGA 1 = +/-4.096 V, 128 SPS, single shot)

||Signal||ADC||Bus||AIN||Conversion||
| UV_RIGHT (right panel photoresistor) | U6 | i2c-0 | 0 | volts only (~2.8 V dark, lower when lit) |
| TEMP_RIGHT (right panel NTC) | U6 | i2c-0 | 1 | NTC -> deg C |
| UV_LEFT (left panel photoresistor) | U6 | i2c-0 | 2 | volts only |
| TEMP_LEFT (left panel NTC) | U6 | i2c-0 | 3 | NTC -> deg C |
| TEMP_BACK | U7 | i2c-1 | 0 | NTC -> deg C |
| TEMP_DOOR | U7 | i2c-1 | 1 | NTC -> deg C |
| TEMP_CHAMBER | U7 | i2c-1 | 2 | NTC -> deg C -> {{ChamberTempCalibration.Correct}} |
| N2 pressure (SMC ISE20A analog, via R86 120 R) | U7 | i2c-1 | 3 | {{PressureConversion.Convert}} |

Volts = raw(int16) * FS[pga] / 32768, FS = {0: 6.144, 1: 4.096, 2: 2.048, 3: 1.024, 4: 0.512, 5: 0.256}. NTC (Murata NCP21XV103J03RA, 10 k pull-up to 3.3 V): R = 10000*v/(3.3-v); 1/T = 1/298.15 + ln(R/10000)/3934; degC = T-273.15; v<=0 or v>=3.3 -> null (open/short). 1.65 V = 25.0 degC. Pressure (shipped config analog_voltage): MPa linear through (1.0 V, 0.0 MPa) and (5.0 V, 1.0 MPa) i.e. 4 V per MPa; bar = MPa*10; saturated above 3.2 V (Mpa null); On = MPa >= set_point_mpa (0.1).

*CM5 GPIO* (RP1 {{/dev/gpiochipN}}, chip auto-detected, usually 0)

||GPIO||Dir||Function||Notes||
| 6 | out | {{4DA_BOFA_EN}} extraction fan 24 V high-side MOSFET (J24 pin 31) | opened LOW; {{bofa.enable_gpio}} |
| 8 | out (PIO / soft PWM) | damper servo MG90S via inverting transistor Q16 | {{servo.gpio}}, signal_inverted=true |
| 12 | out (PIO) | RGB status strip TM1903/WS2811, 21 LEDs, RGB order | {{rgb.gpio}} |
| 13 | out | nitrogen solenoid valve | active high, opened LOW |
| 16 | out | 450 nm LED supply SSR (K1) | {{led_power.ssr_450nm}} |
| 17 | out | voltage-routing line; kept LOW in both modes (HIGH kills the door DIM 12 V rail) | {{led_power.routing}}, read back |
| 18 | in, no pull (ext. R134 4.75k pull-up) | {{4DA_BOFA_PRESENT}} (J24 pin 12) | {{bofa.present_gpio}}, active low assumed |
| 19, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26 | in, pull-up, rising-edge counted | fan tachometers (LEFT, HEATER, DOOR, RIGHT, BACK, COOLING) | 2 pulses / revolution |
| 20 | out | 405 nm LED supply SSR (K2) | {{led_power.ssr_405nm}} |
| 27 | in, no pull (ext. R46) | door sensor; HIGH = closed, LOW = open | {{door_sensor.open_level}} 0 |

Servo pulse: logical angle a' = 180 - angle; pulse_us = round(500 + a'/180*1900); logical 0 deg = 2400 us, 90 deg = 1450 us, 180 deg = 500 us; period 20000 us. Damper open = 0 deg (2400 us), closed = 90 deg (1450 us) from {{cooling.damper_open_angle}} / {{damper_closed_angle}}.

*Notes on docs vs code* (code wins, the rebuild must follow the code): {{docs/02-hardware-map.md}} still says damper open = 90 / closed = 0 (code + config: open 0 / closed 90 since 2026-10-26); it says {{ReadRpm}} = delta since last call (code: shared >=1 s window via {{TachRateTracker}}); it lists old FAN_HEATER nominal RPMs (code: 30:2363, 50:3669, 80:5227, 100:5925); it says door magnet released after 2.0 s (the hardware layer does NOT auto-release; the release timer lives in Application-Process {{CureController.OpenDoor}}); it mentions {{busy}} purple comet (shipped config: blue solid). {{Pca9685.SetFrequency}} exists but is never called in production: the chip runs at its power-on prescale (doc: ~200 Hz). column4: sCureBox - Application - process engine
column5:
h3. Application: process engine — overview

The process engine lives in {{src/SCureBox.Application}} (project {{SCureBox.Application.csproj}}, .NET 10) and turns the
hardware facade ({{SCureBox.Hardware.IHardwareSystem}}, {{IHardwareConfig}} — area *Hardware*) into the machine-level
operations the API and UI use. Layers, bottom-up:

# *Device loops* ({{Devices/}}): {{HeatingLoop}} (PI + delta-sigma on the heater SSR, own thread, heater-fan run-on) and
   {{CoolingLoop}} (fixed-duty chamber fan + damper open until target, own thread). Both are driven by a {{TimeProvider}}
   so tests run on {{FakeTimeProvider}}. {{PeriodicWorker}} = dedicated thread ticking every N s.
# *CureController* ({{Process/}}, namespace {{SCureBox.Application.ProcessControl}}): the {{ICureController}}
   command surface. Composes heating, cooling, UV (LED panels), damper, fans, nitrogen valve, BOFA fume extractor, door
   magnet, RGB override; runs the start pre-flights (sensors, frozen reading, critical fans, LED fans, chamber cooling
   fan); builds the {{/api/state}} snapshot ({{MachineState}}).
# *Supervision* ({{Supervision/}}): {{SupervisionService}} (1 Hz tick) feeds {{SupervisionState}} (thread-safe holder of the
   Domain evaluators: sensors, frozen reading, no-heat, fan health, LED heating, UV light) and applies consequences
   (stop all, heater off, restart after 9006), runs the N2 interlock, and the door watchdog.
# *RecipeRunner* ({{Recipe/}}): server-side program execution on a 1 s tick, driving the Domain {{RecipeStateMachine}}
   and translating its commands into {{ICureController}} calls; records telemetry, phase timings, run alerts.
# *Status strip* ({{Status/}}): {{StatusLedService}} (RGB strip ladder + animation), {{InternetWatcher}}, {{StripStatus}}.
# *DI* ({{ProcessServiceCollectionExtensions.AddSCureBoxProcess}}).

Shared conventions:
* Every command returns {{SCureBox.Domain.Errors.OpResult(bool Ok, string Message, int? Code)}} — never throws.
  {{OpResult.FromRefusal(reason)}}: a reason starting {{"[NNNN] "}} yields {{Code = NNNN}} and the message without the prefix,
  else {{Code = 6015}} ({{ErrorCodes.HardwareRefused}}). {{OpResult.SplitCode(reason)}} returns {{(int? code, string message)}}.
* Error codes used in this area (all from {{ErrorCodes}}, area *Domain*): 6015 HardwareRefused, 6016 DoorAbort,
  7001 InvalidTemperature, 7002 InvalidIntensity, 9006 TempReadingFrozen, 9007 HeaterNotHeating, 9008 N2PressureTooHigh,
  9009 N2NoSupply, 9010-9014 per-sensor disconnected (Chamber, Left, Right, Back, Door), 9015 N2FlowBlocked,

column4: sCureBox - Application - platform, persistence, reports
column5:
h3. Application: platform, persistence, reports — overview

This area is the "platform" half of {{src/SCureBox.Application}} (namespace roots {{SCureBox.Application.Persistence}}, {{SCureBox.Application.Platform}}, {{SCureBox.Application.Reports}}). It has no UI and no hardware drivers of its own; it gives the rest of the system:

* *Durable data* — a directory of JSON files ({{DataOptions.DataDir}}, env {{SCURE_DATA_DIR}}, default {{<app>/data}}) written power-cut-safe (tmp + fsync + rename), with an optional PostgreSQL backend (env {{DATABASE_URL}}) chosen once at boot and falling back to JSON when the database is not usable. Bundled read-only config lives in {{DataOptions.ConfigDir}} (default {{<app>/config}}: {{presets.json}}, {{errors.json}}, {{system.json}}, {{origin.json}}, {{versions.json}}, {{components.json}}).
* *Platform services* — external commands without a shell, power/clock/version/USB exports, network status/diagnostics/static IP, signed {{.scu}} software update (or the Origin supervisor on :8080), outbound-only cloud sync agent, component ON-hour counters, LED calibration factors, BOFA extractor setting, the serial-number backup on a removable card, USB NFC reader detection + Eccel Pepper C2 tag reading, developer event log.
* *Reports* — self-contained HTML cure report (inline SVG charts + timing diagram), HDT calibration report (HTML + CSV), and the save-to-store + export-to-USB helper.

Project: {{src/SCureBox.Application/SCureBox.Application.csproj}} (net10.0 via Directory.Build props; packages {{Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting.Abstractions}} 10.0.13, {{Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions}} 10.0.13, {{Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions}} 10.0.13, {{Microsoft.Extensions.Options}} 10.0.13, {{Npgsql}} 10.0.3; references {{SCureBox.Domain}}, {{SCureBox.Hardware}}; {{InternalsVisibleTo SCureBox.Application.Tests}}). Tests: {{tests/SCureBox.Application.Tests}} (xunit 2.9.3, Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing 10.11.0 {{FakeTimeProvider}}).

Cross-cutting rules for every ticket:
# Every file write of durable state goes through {{AtomicFile}} (PLAT-01). Readers are tolerant: missing/corrupt file = defaults + a {{LogWarning}}, never an exception at boot.
# External tools are run through {{ProcessRunner}} (PLAT-05): {{ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList}}, never a shell, never throws.
# Off-Linux (developer PC) every machine action (reboot, clock, nmcli, mount, install.sh) is *simulated* and returns success with a "simulated" message, so the UI is exercisable on Windows.
# Error codes come from {{SCureBox.Domain.Errors.ErrorCodes}} (Domain area, mirror of {{config/errors.json}}). Codes used here: 3001 SerialRestoreFailed ("Serial Number Restore Failed", critical), 4003 SdBackupWriteFailed (warning), 9006 (frozen reading latch, raised by Process), 9052 NfcReaderNotDetected (warning), 9080 UnknownDiagnosticTool, 9081 NoUsbDrive ("No Disk-on-Key Connected"), 9082 UsbWriteFailed, 9083 LogExportFailed, 9084 NetworkError ("Network Status Unavailable"), 9085 DiagnosticFailed, 9086 UpdateFailed (critical), 9087 NoUpdatePackage. {{OpResult(bool Ok, string Message, int? Code = null)}} with {{Success(msg)}} / {{Fail(msg, code?)}} is a Domain record.
# Log prefixes used: {{[DATA]}}, {{[DB]}}, {{[BOOT]}}, {{[SYSTEM]}}, {{[NET]}}, {{[UPDATE]}}, {{[CLOUD]}}, {{[COUNTERS]}}, {{[LED-CAL]}}, {{[NFC]}}, {{[DEV]}}, {{[REPORT]}}.
# Not in this area (despite the area description): there is *no* Wi-Fi, licensing or NetBird-enrolment code in {{SCureBox.Application}}. NetBird appears only as "tunnel IP" detection (PLAT-09). Origin sign-in ({{config/origin.json}} consumer {{OriginBrowserSignIn}}), {{system.json}} consumer ({{UiSettingsStore}}) and {{versions.json}} consumer ({{VersionsDialogViewModel}}) live in *Native UI*; their file formats are documented in PLAT-16. NetBird enrolment is *Deploy-Ops* ({{deploy/netbird-enroll.sh}}).

column4: sCureBox - DVT bench & HDT
column5:
h3. DVT bench & HDT — overview

The DVT (design verification testing) and HDT (heat deflection test / material calibration) area gives engineers machine-side, machine-clock instruments for verification tests and material calibration. It has two halves:

# *Inside the firmware process* ({{scurebox}}, API on :3001, project {{SCureBox.Application}}):
** {{DvtBench}}: one lock for the shared bench instruments (the LEDs and the StarBright meter). Holds can be leased.
** The UV power meter: the Ophir StarBright over libusb, plus a simulated meter.
** {{UvSweep}}: UV linearity sweep (DVT-OPT-001 at 405 nm, DVT-OPT-002 at 450 nm).
** {{UvOffTiming}}: UV off when the door opens (DVT-SAF-008 step 2).
** {{DvtHang}}: firmware hang on purpose, so the output watchdog has to cut (DVT-SAF-010).
** {{RemoteConfirm}}: a test asked for from the cloud must be confirmed at the machine.
** The PicoLog TC-08 thermocouple probe (native {{libusbtc08}}) and its simulation.
** {{HdtCalibration}}: material HDT calibration, a 10..90 % LED power ladder.
# *The separate DVT bench process* ({{scurebox --dvt-bench}}, :3002, systemd {{scurebox-dvt-bench.service}}, code in {{SCureBox.Application/Dvt/Bench}} + {{SCureBox.Api/Bench}}). It talks to the firmware only over HTTP and keeps measuring even when the firmware is frozen, killed or restarting:
** {{BenchRecorder}}: a generic recording at 1..20 Hz of TC-08 + StarBright + firmware state, with marks and auto-events.
** {{BenchRunner}}: runs one whole catalog test (DVT-SAF-002, heater thermistor open) on its own clock, with prompts to the operator.
** {{SimulatedBenchWorld}}: a complete fake machine for the tests and for {{SCURE_SIMULATE=1}}.

Instrument ownership rules (they hold across all tickets):
* The TC-08 is normally open in the firmware ({{PicoLogTc08Probe}}). The bench takes it with {{POST /api/dev/picolog/release}} and gives it back with {{POST /api/dev/picolog/resume}}.
* Two handles on the StarBright at the same time wedge it (LIBUSB_ERROR_IO). Inside one process, a static semaphore admits one conversation at a time. Across processes, the bench claims the firmware's {{DvtBench}} on a 30 s lease ({{/api/dvt/bench/claim}}) and renews it every 10 s.
* Every exit path of every measurement leaves the LEDs and the heater OFF.

All "now" values come from an injected {{TimeProvider}}, so tests drive a {{FakeTimeProvider}}. Blocking waits use the extension {{TimeProvider.Wait(TimeSpan, CancellationToken) -> bool cancelled}} (DVT-01).

Ticket list:
* DVT-01: DVT bench lock, clock waits and UV meter abstraction (StarBright libusb + simulated).
* DVT-02: UV linearity sweep + meter endpoints.
* DVT-03: UV-off-on-door-open timing.
* DVT-04: Firmware hang for the watchdog test (DvtHang).
* DVT-05: Remote confirmation at the machine (RemoteConfirm).
* DVT-06: PicoLog TC-08 probe (native interop, firmware-side reader, simulation).
* DVT-07: Material HDT calibration (state machine, model, CSV report, LED-calibration math).
* DVT-08: Bench-process contracts, trace math, TC-08 bench source and BenchRecorder.
* DVT-09: BenchRunner (DVT-SAF-002) and SimulatedBenchWorld.
* DVT-10: DVT bench host process (HTTP API, firmware client, safety net, systemd unit).

column4: sCureBox - API
column5:
h3. API — overview

{{SCureBox.Api}} (assembly name {{scurebox}}, namespace root {{SCureBox.Api}}) is the HTTP host of the firmware. It composes the
Hardware, Application-Process and Application-Platform layers into one ASP.NET Core minimal-API {{WebApplication}}, serves the
{{/api}} contract the React kiosk UI and the native Avalonia UI depend on, serves the built React UI as static files with an SPA
fallback, and hosts two safety liveness services (systemd watchdog keep-alive and the output-watchdog heartbeat file). The same
{{ScureApiHost.Build(...)}} is used by the API executable and in-process by the native UI (which adds its own {{/api/ui/*}} routes
through {{IApiEndpointMapper}}).

Global conventions (detailed in API-02):
* Port 3001 (env {{PORT}}) on all interfaces, unless {{ASPNETCORE_URLS}} is set. CORS wide open. No authentication, no PIN, no
  SSE / WebSocket — the UI polls. The only access control is a loopback check on a few DVT routes (API-12).
* Almost every response is HTTP 200, also on logical failure: {{{ok:false, code?, message}}}. Exceptions to 200 are listed per route.
* Command routes take query-string parameters; data routes take JSON bodies (read leniently: bad / empty JSON = "no body").
* An unhandled exception under {{/api}} becomes {{200 {ok:false, message:<exception message>}}}.
* While a DVT hang is active every non-GET/HEAD {{/api/*}} request answers {{409}} except an allow-list (API-12).

column4: sCureBox - Native UI - shell & pages
column5:
h2. 08 — Native UI (src/SCureBox.Ui, pages / shell / services / controls)

Scope of this file: everything in {{src/SCureBox.Ui}} except the dialogs ({{Views/Dialogs}}, {{ViewModels/Dialogs}}, {{Dialogs/}} = {{IDialogService}}, {{DialogService}}, {{DialogViewModel}} — see the "Native UI dialogs" tickets). Dialog view models are referenced here by their exact class name and the result type the pages await.

h3. Native UI — overview

*What it is.* {{scurebox-ui}} is ONE .NET process: it builds the firmware ASP.NET Core host (hardware + process + platform layers, {{/api}} on :3001, systemd READY/WATCHDOG) with {{ScureApiHost.Build(args, b => b.Services.AddSCureBoxUi())}}, starts it, then runs Avalonia 12 on the main thread with the host's {{IServiceProvider}} as the DI root. View models call the in-process services directly ({{ICureController}}, {{IRecipeRunner}}, {{IMaterialStore}}, {{ICureRunStore}}, {{IPrintHistoryStore}}, {{IPhaseTimingStore}}, {{INetworkService}}, {{ISystemService}}, {{INfcReaderDetector}}, {{ILedCalibrationStore}}, {{IComponentCounters}}, {{IHdtCalibration}}, {{ITemperatureProbe}}, {{ICureReportBuilder}}, {{IHdtReportBuilder}}, {{ErrorRegistry}}, {{TimeProvider}}, …). *The UI never calls the HTTP API.* The only HTTP surface this project adds is the QA group {{/api/ui/*}} (UI-08).

*Stack.* {{net10.0}} (from the repo's shared build props — OPEN QUESTION: the csproj itself sets no TargetFramework; take it from Directory.Build.props of the solution), Avalonia 12.1.4 ({{Avalonia}}, {{Avalonia.Desktop}}, {{Avalonia.LinuxFramebuffer}}, {{Avalonia.Themes.Fluent}}, {{Avalonia.Fonts.Inter}}, {{Avalonia.Skia}}, {{Avalonia.HarfBuzz}}, {{Avalonia.Wayland}}), CommunityToolkit.Mvvm 8.4.2 ({{[ObservableProperty]}}, {{[RelayCommand]}} — all VM property / command names below are the generated public names), Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting(.Systemd) 10.0.13. Compiled bindings by default ({{AvaloniaUseCompiledBindingsByDefault=true}}). AssemblyName {{scurebox-ui}}, RootNamespace {{SCureBox.Ui}}, {{InternalsVisibleTo SCureBox.Ui.Tests}}. Project references: {{SCureBox.Application}}, {{SCureBox.Api}}.

*Design surface.* Every screen is laid out on a fixed *1600 x 1000* design surface ({{ShellView}} Width=1600 Height=1000), scaled uniformly into the output by {{ShellScaler}} (Viewbox, letterboxed on black) and rotated 90° when the output is portrait (the 10.1" Touch Display 2 is portrait-native 1200x1920). All sizes in these tickets are design pixels (React spec px x 2).

*Shell layout.* {{ShellView}} = Grid with layers bottom→top: {{PageLayer}} (row 0: {{TopBar}} 96 px high, hidden on full-screen routes; row 1: {{PageHost}} ContentControl bound to {{CurrentPage}}), {{PageFade}} (page crossfade still, disabled by default), {{PageBlur}} (opaque blurred still of the page while a dialog is up), {{DialogHost}} (modal host), {{FloatLayer}} (Canvas for drop-down lists).

Subscriptions to singleton events ({{MachineStateStore.Updated}}, {{AlertService.Changed}}, {{UiSettingsStore.Changed}}, {{DevModeService.Changed}}) are attached in {{OnNavigatedTo}} and detached in {{OnNavigatedFrom}}; timers are stopped in {{OnNavigatedFrom}}.
# Every user-visible string lives in {{Resources/Strings*.cs}} ({{static partial class Strings}} with nested static classes); views use {{{x:Static s:Strings+Group.Name}}}. US English. Titles are white, never blue.

# Error codes used here: 3001 SerialRestoreFailed, 4003 SdBackupWriteFailed, 6015 HardwareRefused, 6016 DoorAbort, 7004 TemperatureStall, 9001 TempSensorDisconnected (family), 9002 FanFailure (family 902x), 9003 LedFanStopped (family 903x), 9004 LedNotHeating (per panel 9040/9041/9044/9045 via {{ErrorCodes.LedNotHeatingOf(panel)}}), 9006 TempReadingFrozen, 9010 ChamberSensorDisconnected, 9016 N2 sensor not reading, 9017 WatchdogTripped, 9051 FanWearWarning (family 906x), 9052 NfcReaderNotDetected, 9081 NoUsbDrive, 9082 UsbWriteFailed, 9083 LogExportFailed, 9084 NetworkError, 9085 DiagnosticFailed, 9089 ApiUnreachable. {{ErrorCodes.IsA(code, family)}} and {{ErrorCodes.Family(code)}} come from Domain.

column4: sCureBox - sCure Cloud portal (Google Apps Script)
column5:
h3. sCure Cloud portal — overview

The sCure Cloud portal is a *Google Apps Script web app* (V8 runtime) whose only storage is *one Google Sheet* ("sCure Cloud data") plus *one Drive folder* ("sCure DVT files") and the Apps Script *CacheService / PropertiesService*. Source folder: {{cloud/google/}} (portal build {{0.9.146}}). It replaced the Fly.io portal {{cloud/portal.py}} (deleted 2026-10); {{Page.html}} is now hand-edited, not generated.

*Files*

||File||Role||In git||
| {{Code.gs}} | the whole server: {{doGet}}, {{doPost}}, every {{portal*}} function the page calls, storage, auth, DVT queue | yes |
| {{Page.html}} | the single-page UI (CSS + markup + script in one file); first {{<script>}} is a {{fetch}} shim onto {{google.script.run}} | yes |
| {{ErrorRegistry.gs}} | {{var ERROR_REGISTRY = {version, codes:{"<code>":{t,v?}}}}} generated by {{build_errors.py}} | yes |
| {{Secrets.gs}} | {{var SECRETS = {password, machineKeys, dvtKey, netbirdToken, netbirdPeers}}} generated by {{build_secrets.py}} | *no* ({{.gitignore}} line 39) |
| {{appsscript.json}} | manifest: scopes, web-app access | yes |
| {{.clasp.json}} / {{.claspignore}} | clasp project binding / push allow-list | yes |
| {{build_errors.py}}, {{build_secrets.py}} | generators | yes |
| {{test_*.cjs}}, {{test_page.py}} | Node (vm fakes / puppeteer-core) and Python (playwright) tests | yes |
| {{*.png}} | screenshots ({{live-simulation.png}}, {{run-window.png}}, {{simulation-howto.png}}) | yes |

*Data flow*

```
CureBox firmware (PLAT-10 CloudSyncAgent) ──POST /exec {machineKey, snapshot | kind:report | kind:delete_reports}──▶ doPost
                                         ◀── {ok, acceptsReports, commands:[{id,type,payload}]} ──────────────────────
DVT tool (DVT/web/dvt-tool.html)  ──POST /exec {machineKey:<DVT key>, kind:"dvt_run"|"dvt_file"|"dvt_catalog"|...}──▶ doPost
DVT runner on a CureBox (DVT/runner/dvt-runner.cjs) ──POST /exec {DVT key, kind:"dvt_runner_hello"|"dvt_next"|"dvt_events"|"dvt_update"}─▶ doPost
                                                     ── firmware RemoteConfirm (DVT-05) gates every start AT the machine
Browser ──GET /exec──▶ doGet ──▶ Page.html ──google.script.run.portal*(token,…)──▶ Code.gs ──▶ Sheet / Drive / Cache
Browser ──GET /exec?report=…&m=…&t=… | ?dvtfile=…&t=… | ?code=…&state=… (Google OAuth return)──▶ doGet
Code.gs ──UrlFetchApp──▶ api.netbird.io (read-only peers) ; oauth2.googleapis.com/token (sign-in)
```

Machine commands are *data-only by design* ({{upsert_program}}, {{delete_program}}, {{send_print}}, {{delete_print}}); no command actuates hardware. DVT tests can be *requested* from the site but only start after someone presses Start on the CureBox screen (runner → firmware RemoteConfirm, DVT-05).

*Sheets* (created by {{book_()}} on first use; header row frozen; the default {{Sheet1}} / {{גיליון1}} is deleted)

| {{dvt_catalog}} | {{updated, catalog}} | one data row; catalog JSON split over B.. |
| {{dvt_requests}} | {{id, machine, unit, testId, status, requested, started, finished, line, prompt, answer, runIds, verdict, act}} | {{act}} migrated in (0.9.145) |

*Views of the page* (built by the other two ticket ranges; server functions they call are in CLOUD-04): top navigation {{Overview}}, {{Machine}}, {{DVT}}, {{Race}}, {{Compare}}, {{Errors}} ({{data-view}} = {{overview|machines|dvt|race|compare|errors}}) plus the header's People screen and dialogs (program editor, Send Simulated Print, DVT guide / simulation). Shell, Overview, Machines, Race, Compare, phone layout = CLOUD-20..39; Errors, DVT, Programs + editor, People, Simulation, other dialogs = CLOUD-40..59.

Cross-cutting server rules (every ticket):
# All times stored as *unix seconds* ({{now_() = Date.now()/1000}}, fractional) unless stated ({{audit.unix}} and {{users.lastLogin/added}} are floored).
# Every write path takes {{LockService.getScriptLock().waitLock(20000)}} and releases it in {{finally}}.
# Endpoints never answer HTTP error codes (Apps Script cannot): failures are {{{ok:false, message}}} with HTTP 200. Page functions return {{null}} for "not signed in".
# Long text (JSON, HTML) is split into {{CELL_MAX = 45000}}-character chunks over consecutive cells and joined back on read; on rewrite, a shorter value pads the row with {{''}} up to the sheet's last column so old chunks are cleared.
# Never store a machine key ({{delete d.machineKey}} before storing). Never copy secrets into source; see CLOUD-02.

column4: OPS-02 Versioning convention (VERSION, versions.json, GITINFO)
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Versioning
*Blocked by:* OPS-01, API-01, API-10, UIDLG-17
*Blocks:* OPS-03, OPS-14, OPS-15
*Relates to:* PLAT-06, PLAT-16, UI-19
*Implements:* EP-01, EP-02, EP-11, REQ-13

*Project / folder:* {{VERSION}}, {{config/versions.json}}, {{CHANGE_SUMMARY.md}}; consumed by {{src/SCureBox.Api}} and {{src/SCureBox.Ui}}
*Goal:* One product version string with a release-notes registry. Every change bumps the version and adds an entry. Build scripts stamp the git commit next to the executables, and the running unit reports the version through {{/api/system/version}} and the Settings > Versions modal.
*Depends on:* OPS-01. Api ({{/api/system/version}}, {{scurebox --version}}), Native UI (Versions dialog).
*Files to create:*
* {{VERSION}}: one line, semver {{MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH}} (here {{1.0.152}}), trailing newline allowed.
* {{config/versions.json}}: the release-notes registry.
* {{CHANGE_SUMMARY.md}}: a free-form, human-written summary of the changes (no tooling reads it).
*Public contract:*
* {{config/versions.json}} = {{{"_comment": "<rule text>", "history": [ {"version": "1.0.152", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "notes": ["...", "..."]}, ... ]}}}, newest first. The repo has 265 entries, from 1.0.152 back to 0.1.0 (2026-08-06). The {{_comment}} text is: "sCure version registry - newest first. On every release: bump the VERSION file at the repo root AND add an entry here (version, date, notes). The Settings > Versions modal shows this list."
* {{GITINFO}} (generated, never committed): two lines, the short commit hash ({{git rev-parse --short HEAD}}) and the commit date ({{git log -1 --format=%cs}}, YYYY-MM-DD). The build scripts write it to {{src/SCureBox.Api/GITINFO}} and copy it to the payload root.
* The {{SCureBox.Api.csproj}} content items copy {{../../VERSION}} to the output root as {{VERSION}} and {{../../config/**}} to {{config/}} (CopyToOutput and CopyToPublish = PreserveNewest).
* Version resolution at runtime (Api / Application-Platform): read the first line of {{<AppContext.BaseDirectory>/VERSION}}. If it is missing or empty, fall back to {{AssemblyInformationalVersion}} (the part before {{+}}), then to the assembly version (3 parts), then to {{"unknown"}}. {{/api/system/version}} returns {{{appVersion, gitCommit, gitDate, lastBoot, os, kernel, python:null, runtime, emmcSerial}}}. {{gitCommit}} and {{gitDate}} come from {{GITINFO}}, or null when it is missing.
* {{scurebox --version}} prints the same app version and exits.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# Every code change bumps {{VERSION}} (normally the PATCH number) and inserts a new object at index 0 of {{history}} with the same version, today's date and one or more notes. Notes are full sentences: what changed and why (often "user, <date>"), followed by a "Tests: ..." note that names the tests that prove it.
# Commit messages follow {{type(scope): summary - v1.0.N}} (for example {{fix: ... - v1.0.86}}, {{feat(ui): ... - v1.0.81}}). Older commits used {{v1.0.N: summary}}. A commit that covers several versions writes {{v1.0.87..1.0.106}}.
# {{Directory.Build.props}} {{Version}} stays {{1.0.0}}. It is not synchronised with {{VERSION}}.
# The release artifact names carry the version read from {{VERSION}}: {{scurebox-<v>-linux-arm64.tar.gz}}, {{scurebox-<v>-origin-app.tgz}}, {{scurebox-<v>-cm5.img}}, {{sCureBox-Installer-<v>.zip}}, {{sCureBox-Demo-Setup-<v>.exe}}. Downstream tools take the version from the tarball name: the second {{-}}-separated token.
# {{ui/dist/config/versions.json}} is a separate file with the same shape: the web UI's own registry (sCure-A 0.9.4). It is not the firmware registry. See OPS-11.
*Configuration:* none.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* {{VERSION}} and {{history[0].version}} are equal.
* {{scurebox --version}} prints the VERSION content.
* After {{publish.ps1}}, the payload root holds {{VERSION}} and {{GITINFO}}, and {{/api/system/version}} shows {{gitCommit}} and {{gitDate}}.
* With {{GITINFO}} removed, {{gitCommit}} and {{gitDate}} are null and the endpoint still answers.
*Tests:* {{tests/SCureBox.Application.Tests/Platform/SystemServiceTests.cs}} (writes a temporary {{VERSION}} "0.9.1" and expects appVersion 0.9.1); {{tests/SCureBox.Api.Tests/StaticUiTests.cs}} ({{/config/versions.json}} is served); QA row {{sys_version}} (appVersion is x.y.z and every key is present).
*Reference (source):* {{VERSION}}, {{config/versions.json}}, {{CHANGE_SUMMARY.md}}, {{src/SCureBox.Api/SCureBox.Api.csproj}}, {{src/SCureBox.Api/Infrastructure/CommandLine.cs}} (ReadAppVersion), {{src/SCureBox.Application/Platform/SystemService.cs}} (Version/ReadAppVersion), {{src/SCureBox.Ui/ViewModels/Dialogs/VersionsDialogViewModel.cs}}, {{deploy/publish.ps1}}

---

column4: OPS-03 Release build: publish.ps1 and the linux-arm64 payload
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Deploy & OS image, Software update, Data & persistence
*Blocked by:* OPS-01, OPS-02, API-01, UI-01, HW-08
*Blocks:* OPS-04, OPS-12, OPS-13
*Relates to:* PLAT-08, PLAT-03, PLAT-16
*Implements:* OD-75, OD-50, OD-49, EP-10, REQ-21

*Project / folder:* {{deploy/publish.ps1}}, {{deploy/deploy-to-pi.ps1}}, {{deploy/keys/}}, {{deploy/db/}}
*Goal:* Build the self-contained linux-arm64 release, which is both executables plus everything {{install.sh}} needs, as one tarball. The tarball is the input of every installer path: SSH deploy, image build, and the field installer.
*Depends on:* OPS-01, OPS-02. Api and Native UI (the projects being published), Hardware ({{src/SCureBox.Hardware/native}}).
*Files to create:* {{deploy/publish.ps1}}; {{deploy/deploy-to-pi.ps1}}; {{deploy/keys/scure-update.pub}}; {{deploy/db/schema.sql}}; {{deploy/db/seed_presets.sql}}.
*Public contract:*
* {{publish.ps1 [-Runtime linux-arm64] [-SkipTests]}} writes {{deploy/out/scurebox-<version>-<Runtime>.tar.gz}}, which holds one top-level folder {{scurebox-<version>-<Runtime>/}}.
* Payload layout:
** {{scurebox}}, {{scurebox-ui}} plus their DLLs and the .NET runtime (self-contained, not single-file, {{DebugType=none}}, {{UseAppHost=true}})
** {{wwwroot/}} (ui/dist)
** {{config/}}
** {{VERSION}}, {{GITINFO}}
** {{deploy/}}: a copy of the repo deploy folder without {{out}}, {{image/cache}}, {{image/out}}, {{image/input}}, {{*netbird-setup-key*}}, {{*.img}}, {{*.img.xz}}, {{*.img.zip}}
** {{native/}}: a copy of {{src/SCureBox.Hardware/native}}, which includes {{build-pio-helpers.sh}}, {{pio_*.c}} and {{linux-arm64/}}
** {{keys/scure-update.pub}}
* {{deploy-to-pi.ps1 -Host <ip> [-User testingpi] [-Key ~/.ssh/scure_pi] [-Tarball] [-SudoPassword <securestring>] [-NoKiosk] [-Reboot]}} copies the newest tarball to {{/tmp}}, extracts it and runs {{sudo ./deploy/install.sh}}. When a password is given it is echoed to {{sudo -S}}; otherwise it uses {{sudo -n}}.
* {{keys/scure-update.pub}}: a PEM "PUBLIC KEY" (an RSA 4096-bit SubjectPublicKeyInfo, 814 bytes). It verifies signed {{.scu}} USB update packages. The matching private key is NOT in the repo. It is passed to {{scurebox --make-update-package <folder> <privateKeyPem> <out.scu>}} when a package is built. A rebuild generates its own key pair, commits only the public half, and keeps the private half outside the repo.
* {{deploy/db/schema.sql}}: idempotent PostgreSQL schema ({{CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS}}, {{pgcrypto}}). Tables: resins, materials, cure_profiles, printers, jobs, prints, build_heads, tray_membranes, print_hardware, cure_boxes, cure_sessions, cure_runs (+ JSONB {{sensor_issues}}, {{fan_issues}}, {{run_alerts}} added with {{ALTER ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS}}), cure_run_telemetry (+ {{fan_rpm}} JSONB), cure_reports. Views: v_materials, v_print_history, v_cure_history.
* {{deploy/db/seed_presets.sql}}: one {{WITH ins AS (INSERT INTO materials (ext_id,name,is_preset) ... ON CONFLICT (ext_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id) INSERT INTO cure_profiles ...}} block per preset ({{preset-ST45}}, {{preset-Carbon Fiber}}, ...), with the steps JSON. The Application-Platform persistence layer looks for these files in {{<app>/db}}, then {{<app>/deploy/db}}, then the repo's {{deploy/db}}, and applies them when {{DATABASE_URL}} is set.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# Unless {{-SkipTests}} is given, run {{dotnet test SCureBox.sln -nologo -v q}} first and stop if it fails.
# Write GITINFO (OPS-02). A git failure is not fatal.
# Publish {{src/SCureBox.Api/SCureBox.Api.csproj}}, then {{src/SCureBox.Ui/SCureBox.Ui.csproj}}, into the same stage folder with {{-c Release -r <rt> --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=false -p:DebugType=none -p:UseAppHost=true}}.
# Copy deploy/ with robocopy, excluding the folders and files above. Robocopy exit codes below 8 are success. A 1.3 GB OS image once ended up in a release and the boot partition could not hold it, so image files are always excluded.
# Rewrite every {{*.sh}} in the stage with LF line endings, UTF-8 without BOM.
# Create the tar with Windows' own {{%SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe}} (bsdtar), run from {{deploy/out}}. A Git-for-Windows tar mangles Windows output paths.
# Print the tarball size in MB.
*Configuration:* none. The NetBird key and passwords are never part of the payload.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* The tarball has exactly one top-level folder.
* {{scurebox}}, {{scurebox-ui}}, {{wwwroot/index.html}}, {{config/components.json}}, {{deploy/install.sh}}, {{native/build-pio-helpers.sh}}, {{keys/scure-update.pub}}, {{VERSION}} are present.
* No {{*.img*}} or {{*netbird-setup-key*}} file is in the tarball.
* Every {{.sh}} in it has no CR characters.
* A failing test stops the publish unless {{-SkipTests}} is given.
*Tests:* manual. {{tar -tzf}} the output and check the list above, then {{install.sh}} on a unit (OPS-04).
*Reference (source):* {{deploy/publish.ps1}}, {{deploy/deploy-to-pi.ps1}}, {{deploy/keys/scure-update.pub}}, {{deploy/db/schema.sql}}, {{deploy/db/seed_presets.sql}}, {{src/SCureBox.Api/Infrastructure/CommandLine.cs}}, {{src/SCureBox.Application/Platform/UpdateService.cs}}, {{src/SCureBox.Application/Persistence/PostgresDatabaseInitializer.cs}}

---

column4: OPS-04 On-device installer install.sh
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Deploy & OS image, Network & NetBird, Kiosk web UI, DVT bench
*Blocked by:* OPS-03, OPS-05, OPS-06, OPS-07, OPS-08, OPS-09, OPS-10, HW-08
*Blocks:* OPS-12, OPS-13
*Relates to:* DVT-06, DVT-10, PLAT-09
*Implements:* OD-75, OD-77, OD-16, REQ-21

*Project / folder:* {{deploy/install.sh}}, {{deploy/networkmanager-scurebox.conf}}
*Goal:* A single idempotent root script, run from an extracted release. It installs the application to {{/opt/scurebox}}, sets up the boot configuration, display, splash, systemd services, remote access, network tolerance and the DVT drivers, and restarts everything. The image first boot, the SSH deploy and the field installer all use it.
*Depends on:* OPS-03, OPS-05, OPS-06, OPS-07, OPS-08, OPS-09, OPS-10.
*Files to create:* {{deploy/install.sh}}; {{deploy/networkmanager-scurebox.conf}}.
*Public contract:*
* {{sudo ./deploy/install.sh [--ui native|browser] [--no-kiosk] [--reboot|--no-reboot] [--payload DIR] [--netbird-key KEY] [--no-netbird]}}. Defaults: {{--ui native}}, kiosk on, no reboot, NetBird on, payload = the parent of the script's directory. An unknown option prints "unknown option X" and exits 2. If not run as root, it prints "run as root (sudo)" and exits 1. If the payload has no {{./scurebox}}, it exits 1.
* Log lines are prefixed {{[install] }}. Callers look for these substrings to tell that the boot config changed: "scurebox fragment", "Touch Display 2 profile", "Plymouth theme".
* {{networkmanager-scurebox.conf}} is installed to {{/etc/NetworkManager/conf.d/90-scurebox-wired.conf}}. Content: section {{[connection-scurebox-wired]}}, {{match-device=interface-name:eth0}}, {{ipv4.dhcp-timeout=2147483647}}.
*Behaviour & rules (in order):*
# {{chmod +x}} the payload's {{scurebox}}, {{deploy/*.sh}}, {{deploy/kiosk/*.sh}}, {{native/*.sh}}. Errors are ignored, because a tarball from Windows loses the mode bits.
# Disable and stop the legacy {{scure.service}} and {{scure-io-safe.service}} when they are enabled (the old Python firmware used the same port 3001). Then stop {{scurebox.service}}.
# {{mkdir -p /opt/scurebox /etc/scurebox /var/lib/scurebox /var/lib/scurebox/logs}}. Run {{rsync -a --delete --exclude data payload/ → /opt/scurebox/}}. If rsync fails, use {{rm -rf}} and {{cp -a}}. Then chmod again. Seed {{/etc/scurebox/components.json}} from {{config/components.json}} only when it does not exist. Run {{ln -sfn /var/lib/scurebox /opt/scurebox/data}}.
# Run {{raspi-config nonint do_i2c 0}} (non-fatal). Boot config is {{/boot/firmware/config.txt}}, or {{/boot/config.txt}}. Append {{config-txt-fragment.txt}} when the file has no {{>>> scurebox}} marker. Append {{display-10inch.txt}} when the file has no {{vc4-kms-dsi-ili79600-10-1inch}}.
# A/B images. For each of {{/dev/disk/by-partlabel/boot_a}} and {{boot_b}} that exists: use its current mount point and remount it rw, or mount it as vfat on a temporary directory. When its {{config.txt}} (case-insensitive name) has no line starting {{dtoverlay=vc4-kms-dsi-ili79600-10-1inch}}, append {{[all]}} plus the display profile, {{sync}}, and log "A/B: 10.1" Touch Display 2 profile added to <slot>". Unmount a temporary mount afterwards.
# PIO helpers. When {{gcc}} exists: if {{/usr/local/src/utils/piolib}} is missing, run {{git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/raspberrypi/utils /usr/local/src/utils}}. Then run {{PIOLIB=/usr/local/src/utils/piolib bash /opt/scurebox/native/build-pio-helpers.sh /opt/scurebox/native}}. A failure is logged ("servo falls back to software PWM") and is not fatal. OPEN QUESTION: {{build-pio-helpers.sh}} reads {{PIOLIB_SRC}}, not {{PIOLIB}}, and treats {{$1}} only as {{install}}. In practice it clones piolib again into {{/tmp/rpi-utils}} and builds into its own directory ({{/opt/scurebox/native}}). Decide whether to fix the variable name.
# systemd UI mode. If {{--ui native}} is chosen but {{/opt/scurebox/scurebox-ui}} is missing, fall back to browser mode and log it. Always install {{scurebox-io-safe.service}} and run {{mkdir -p /var/log/scure}}.
** native: install {{scurebox-ui.service}}; {{disable --now}} and delete {{scurebox-kiosk.service}} and {{scurebox.service}}; daemon-reload; enable io-safe and ui; restart io-safe (errors ignored) and ui; set kiosk off.
** browser: install {{scurebox.service}}; disable and delete {{scurebox-ui.service}}; enable and restart io-safe and scurebox.
# Plymouth. When {{plymouth-set-default-theme}} exists: copy {{deploy/plymouth/scurebox/*}} to {{/usr/share/plymouth/themes/scurebox/}}, then run {{plymouth-set-default-theme -R scurebox}} (fallback: without {{-R}}). cmdline is {{/boot/firmware/cmdline.txt}}, or {{/boot/cmdline.txt}}. Join it into one line. Remove these tokens: {{ console=tty1}}, {{ quiet}}, {{ splash}}, {{ plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles}}, {{ logo.nologo}}, {{ vt.global_cursor_default=0}}, {{ loglevel=N}}, {{ consoleblank=N}}. Then append {{ console=tty3 quiet splash plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles logo.nologo vt.global_cursor_default=0 loglevel=0 consoleblank=0}}. Running it twice gives the same line.
# Native display ownership (native mode): {{disable --now lightdm.service}}, {{mask getty@tty1.service}}, {{systemctl set-default multi-user.target}}, {{raspi-config nonint do_blanking 1}}.
# Browser kiosk (kiosk on and a uid-1000 user exists). Install {{kiosk/labwc/rc.xml}} to {{/etc/scurebox/labwc/rc.xml}} and create an empty {{/etc/scurebox/labwc/autostart}}. Install {{chromium-policy.json}} as {{/etc/chromium/policies/managed/scurebox.json}}. Render {{scurebox-kiosk.service}} with sed: {{__KIOSK_USER__}} = the user name, {{__KIOSK_UID__}} = {{1000}}, {{__KIOSK_HOME__}} = the home directory. Add the user to the groups video, input, render, tty (where they exist). Disable lightdm, run {{set-default graphical.target}}, enable and restart the kiosk, and turn blanking off.
# NetBird (unless {{--no-netbird}}). Install {{scurebox-netbird-enroll.service}}. With {{--netbird-key}}, write it to {{/etc/scurebox/netbird-setup-key}} under umask 077. If that file or {{/boot/firmware/netbird-setup-key}} (or {{/boot/netbird-setup-key}}) is non-empty: enable the enroll service and run {{netbird-enroll.sh}} (with {{set +e}}). On exit 0, disable the service. Otherwise log "...retries every minute" and run {{systemctl start --no-block}} on it. Without a key and with netbird installed, log the {{Management:}} and {{NetBird IP:}} lines of {{netbird status}}.
# Output watchdog. When {{scurebox}} and the unit file exist: install, enable and restart {{scurebox-watchdog.service}}, then log {{systemctl is-active}}.
# When {{/etc/NetworkManager}} exists: install the wired conf and run {{nmcli general reload conf}}. Do not force a reconnect, so an install over SSH never cuts itself off.
# PicoLog TC-08 driver. File {{libusbtc08_2.0.151-1r6217_arm64.deb}}, SHA-256 {{26c85ce1365064164002ec6d0e5edcdd2b5a36cdde61c000c9bf55b27309ed27}}, URL {{https://labs.picotech.com/rc/picoscope7/debian/pool/main/libu/libusbtc08/<deb>}}. Skip when {{dpkg -s libusbtc08}} succeeds, and skip on a non-arm64 system. Use {{deploy/vendor/<deb>}} when it is shipped; otherwise download it with curl ({{--max-time 120}}). Check the checksum with {{sha256sum -c}}, then {{dpkg -i}} and {{ldconfig}}. Every failure is logged and is not fatal. No apt source is added.
# DVT bench: install, enable and restart {{scurebox-dvt-bench.service}} (a failure is logged), then log {{http://localhost:3002/bench/status}}.
# Log "done (ui=<mode>)…". Reboot when {{--reboot}} was given. Exit 0.
*Configuration:* the command-line flags above. The uid-1000 user is the kiosk user.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* After a run in native mode: {{/opt/scurebox/data}} resolves to {{/var/lib/scurebox}}. {{scurebox-ui}}, {{scurebox-io-safe}}, {{scurebox-watchdog}} and {{scurebox-dvt-bench}} are enabled and active. {{scurebox.service}} and {{scurebox-kiosk.service}} do not exist. {{getty@tty1}} is masked.
* A second run appends nothing more to {{config.txt}} or {{cmdline.txt}}.
* An existing {{/etc/scurebox/components.json}} is untouched.

column4: OPS-06 Early-boot IO safe state (scurebox-io-safe + config.txt fragment)
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Safety & watchdog, UV LEDs & wavelength, Deploy & OS image, Nitrogen
*Blocked by:* HW-06, HW-11, HW-12
*Blocks:* OPS-04, OPS-05
*Relates to:* HW-14, HW-09, PLAT-13
*Implements:* OD-16, OD-17, REQ-21

*Project / folder:* {{deploy/scurebox-io-safe.service}}, {{deploy/io-safe-boot.sh}}, {{deploy/config-txt-fragment.txt}}
*Goal:* Make sure the UV SSRs, the wavelength routing line and the LED_SWITCH relay are at rest (off) from the firmware stage of boot until the .NET firmware takes over. This closes the window in which pull-ups could engage an output.
*Depends on:* Hardware (pin map: GPIO16 = 450 nm SSR, GPIO17 = routing / PCA9685 OE, GPIO20 = 405 nm SSR, TCA6424A at i2c-0 0x23, P01 = NFC_RESET, P05 = LED_SWITCH relay K4).
*Files to create:* the three files.
*Public contract:*
* {{config-txt-fragment.txt}}, inserted between markers {{# >>> scurebox}} and {{# <<< scurebox}}:
** {{dtparam=i2c_arm=on}}, {{dtparam=i2c_vc=on}} (with a comment: i2c-1 on GPIO2/3 for U7/U10, i2c-0 on GPIO0/1 for PCA9685/TCA6424A/U6/U8)
** {{gpio=16,17,20=op,dl}}
** {{dtparam=spi=off}} (comment: the damper servo on GPIO8 must not be claimed by SPI)
** {{dtparam=audio=off}}, {{camera_auto_detect=0}}, {{disable_splash=1}}
** {{gpio=27=ip,pn}}
* {{scurebox-io-safe.service}}: {{DefaultDependencies=no}}, {{After=sysinit.target}}, {{Before=scurebox.service}}, {{Type=oneshot}}, {{ExecStart=/bin/bash /opt/scurebox/deploy/io-safe-boot.sh}}, {{RemainAfterExit=yes}}, {{WantedBy=sysinit.target}}. (The scurebox-ui unit orders itself after this unit.)
* {{io-safe-boot.sh}} ({{set -u}}):
## For p in 16 17 20, run {{pinctrl set $p op dl}}.
## When {{i2cset}} exists, run {{i2cset -y 0 0x23 0x04 0x02}} (port-0 output register: P01 = 1, P05 = 0), then {{i2cset -y 0 0x23 0x0C 0xDD}} (port-0 config: P01 and P05 as outputs).
## Ignore every error and always exit 0.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# Write the output register before the config register, so the pins become outputs already at the safe levels.
# The script must never fail the boot.
*Configuration:* none.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* After boot, {{pinctrl get 16,17,20}} reports output low.
* The TCA6424A register 0x0C reads 0xDD and register 0x04 has bit 5 clear and bit 1 set.
* The unit is {{active (exited)}}.
*Tests:* manual on the unit.
*Reference (source):* {{deploy/scurebox-io-safe.service}}, {{deploy/io-safe-boot.sh}}, {{deploy/config-txt-fragment.txt}}

---

*Goal:* Two companion processes, started from the same {{scurebox}} executable, that must keep running when the firmware dies. The output watchdog cuts the heaters and the UV LEDs when the firmware heartbeat goes silent. The DVT bench runs catalog tests with the TC-08 and the StarBright meter on port 3002.
*Depends on:* OPS-04. Hardware ({{OutputWatchdog}}, {{HeartbeatFile}}), Dvt-Hdt ({{DvtBenchHost}}), Api ({{CommandLine.TryRun}}).

** {{--watchdog [--timeout <s>]}} and {{--watchdog --cut-now}}
** {{--dvt-bench [--port 3002] [--firmware <url>]}}
** {{--version}}
** {{--make-update-package <folder> <privateKeyPem> <out.scu>}} (exit 2 on wrong usage, exit 1 on a build failure)
* Heartbeat: the file named by {{SCURE_HEARTBEAT_FILE}} (default {{/run/scurebox-heartbeat}}; {{off}} disables it). It holds one line {{"<Environment.TickCount64 ms> <pid>\n"}} and is replaced atomically (written to {{.tmp}}, then renamed).

*Behaviour & rules:*

column4: OPS-08 NetBird remote access (enroll script + retry unit)
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Network & NetBird, Deploy & OS image
*Blocks:* OPS-04, OPS-12, OPS-13
*Relates to:* PLAT-09, PLAT-05
*Implements:* OD-75, EP-10, REQ-20

*Project / folder:* {{deploy/netbird-enroll.sh}}, {{deploy/scurebox-netbird-enroll.service}}
*Goal:* Install the NetBird WireGuard mesh client and enroll the unit with a one-off setup key, named after its eMMC serial, so that every unit can be reached from anywhere over SSH and the API. The script retries until the unit is online and deletes the key after use.
*Depends on:* OPS-04. Consumers: OPS-12 (key on the boot partition), OPS-13 (key from the PC).
*Files to create:* the script and the unit.
*Public contract:*
* {{sudo deploy/netbird-enroll.sh [--key KEY] [--hostname NAME] [--management-url URL] [--install-only]}}. Key sources, first found wins: {{--key}}, then {{$NETBIRD_SETUP_KEY}}, then {{/etc/scurebox/netbird-setup-key}}, then {{/boot/firmware/netbird-setup-key}} (or {{/boot/netbird-setup-key}}).
* Exit codes: 0 = enrolled, already connected, or nothing to do (no key). 1 = not root. 2 = bad option or bad key format. 75 = no network yet or enrollment failed (retry).
* Key format {{^[A-Za-z0-9-]{8,128}$}}. The key value is never committed or logged.
* Unit: {{After=network-online.target}}, {{Wants=network-online.target}}, {{ConditionPathExists=|/etc/scurebox/netbird-setup-key}}, {{ConditionPathExists=|/boot/firmware/netbird-setup-key}}, {{Type=oneshot}}, {{ExecStart=/bin/bash /opt/scurebox/deploy/netbird-enroll.sh}}, {{Restart=on-failure}}, {{RestartSec=60}}, {{RestartPreventExitStatus=2}}, journal output, {{WantedBy=multi-user.target}}.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# If a non-empty key is on the boot partition (FAT, readable by everyone), move it at once with {{install -m 600 -o root -g root}} to {{/etc/scurebox/netbird-setup-key}} and delete the boot copy.
# Read the key from the etc file when no other source gave one (whitespace stripped). An invalid format logs "unexpected format - refusing" and exits 2.
# When {{netbird}} is not installed:
** no key and not {{--install-only}}: log "remote access not configured" and exit 0.
** otherwise: {{curl -fsSL --max-time 30 https://pkgs.netbird.io/debian/public.key}} (failure → exit 75); {{gpg --dearmor}} it to {{/usr/share/keyrings/netbird-archive-keyring.gpg}}; write {{deb [signed-by=…] https://pkgs.netbird.io/debian stable main}} to {{/etc/apt/sources.list.d/netbird.list}}; {{apt-get update}} limited to that list ({{-o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=… -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=- -o APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0}}); {{apt-get install -y netbird}} (failure → exit 75).
# Run {{netbird service install}} and {{systemctl enable --now netbird.service}} (fallback {{netbird service start}}). Log {{netbird version}}. With {{--install-only}} and no key, exit 0.
# When {{netbird status}} shows {{^Management: Connected}}: log the FQDN and IP, delete both key files, exit 0. When there is no key: exit 0.
# Peer name: {{$(hostname)-<serial>}}. The serial is the first {{/sys/block/mmcblk*/device}} whose {{type}} is {{MMC}}, with spaces removed and a {{0x}} prefix stripped. Run {{timeout 120 netbird up --setup-key KEY --hostname NAME [--management-url URL]}} (failure → exit 75). Poll the status up to 30 times, 2 s apart. Log the FQDN and IP, delete both key files, exit 0.
# The unit stays enrolled through its own WireGuard identity in {{/var/lib/netbird}}. A setup-key peer needs no user login and does not expire.
*Configuration:* setup key (secret), optional management URL.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* With a valid key and network: the unit shows as {{<host>-<serial>}} in the NetBird dashboard and no key file is left anywhere.
* Without network: exit 75, and the service retries every minute.
* With a malformed key: exit 2 and no retry.
* With no key: exit 0 and nothing installed.
*Tests:* manual. {{build-image.py}} and {{install-scurebox.ps1}} validate the key format with the same rule.
*Reference (source):* {{deploy/netbird-enroll.sh}}, {{deploy/scurebox-netbird-enroll.service}}

---

The Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2 (10.1", ILI79600, 1200x1920 native portrait, DSI-1) runs landscape at 1920x1200 on every image, including both slots of a factory A/B image.
*Depends on:* OPS-04 (installs the theme and edits cmdline/config), OPS-12, OPS-13.

* {{plymouth/scurebox/scurebox.script}}, {{plymouth/scurebox/logo.png}}.

** Background top and bottom colour (0.055, 0.078, 0.094) = {{#0e1418}}.
** Logo scaled to window height / 3.2, centred, 30 px above the middle, z = 10.

** Messages: {{Image.Text(text, 0.90,0.92,0.94,1, "Sans 16")}}, centred 24 px under the bar.
** Empty callbacks for quit, password and normal.
* {{patch-display.py --image <.img|.img.xz> [--out F] [--in-place] [--probe] [--check] [--profile F]}}:
** {{--probe}} prints {{factory}} (GPT with partitions named boot_a and boot_b), {{rpios}} (MBR with a FAT partition of type 0x06/0x0B/0x0C/0x0E) or {{unknown}}. It reads only the first 2 MiB, and decompresses at most 8 MiB of a {{.xz}}.
** {{--check}} reports which partitions lack the overlay and exits 1 when any does (it needs an uncompressed image).
** The default output is {{<stem>-display.img}} next to the input. {{.xz}} input is decompressed to it ({{.part}} file, then rename).
** The profile must contain the overlay name, or the tool exits.
* Requires Python 3.10+ and {{pip install pyfatfs "setuptools<81"}}.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# FAT partitions:
** MBR: types 0x06/0x0B/0x0C/0x0E whose boot sector has {{55AA}} and {{FAT}} at offset 0x36 or 0x52.
** GPT: entries with the Basic Data or EFI System type GUID, or a name starting with "boot", and a FAT boot sector.
** A GPT image is detected by MBR type 0xEE, then the "EFI PART" header at LBA 1.
# For each partition with a {{config.txt}} (case-insensitive name): skip it when a stripped line starts with {{dtoverlay=vc4-kms-dsi-ili79600-10-1inch}} (a commented line does not count). Otherwise append {{\n[all]\n<profile>\n}}. pyfatfs cannot rewrite a file in place, so remove the file and write it again. Read it back and verify the overlay is there. Change nothing else.
# {{install.sh}} applies the same rule on a running A/B unit (OPS-04 step 5).
*Configuration:* none.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* An A/B test image gets the profile in both boot_a and boot_b and nothing else changes.
* {{--probe}} tells factory from rpios even for a {{.xz}}.
* An MBR image is patched once; a second run changes nothing.
* An image that already enables the panel is left alone.
*Tests:* {{python deploy/image/test_patch_display.py}} (unittest on synthetic 16 MB FAT16 volumes): {{test_ab_image_gets_the_display_in_both_slots_and_nothing_else_changes}}, {{test_probe_tells_the_factory_ab_image_from_raspberry_pi_os_even_when_compressed}}, {{test_mbr_raspberry_pi_os_image_is_patched_once}}, {{test_an_image_that_already_enables_the_panel_is_left_alone}}, {{test_commented_overlay_does_not_count}}.
*Reference (source):* {{deploy/plymouth/scurebox/*}}, {{deploy/display-10inch.txt}}, {{deploy/image/patch-display.py}}, {{deploy/image/test_patch_display.py}}, {{deploy/image/README.md}}

column4: OPS-10 Browser kiosk shell (Step A: labwc + Chromium)
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Kiosk web UI, Deploy & OS image
*Blocked by:* OPS-05, OPS-11
*Blocks:* OPS-04
*Relates to:* API-04, API-05
*Implements:* OD-73, REQ-21

*Project / folder:* {{deploy/kiosk/}}
*Goal:* In {{--ui browser}} mode, run the React UI full-screen in a locked Chromium on a minimal Wayland compositor (labwc) on tty1. A branded loading page is shown until the API answers. The operator must not be able to leave the app.
*Depends on:* OPS-04, OPS-05 ({{scurebox.service}}), OPS-11.
*Files to create:* {{scurebox-kiosk.service}} (template), {{scurebox-kiosk.sh}}, {{chromium-policy.json}}, {{labwc/rc.xml}}, {{loading.html}}, {{logo.png}}.
*Public contract:*
* Unit template (placeholders {{__KIOSK_USER__}}, {{__KIOSK_UID__}}, {{__KIOSK_HOME__}}):
** {{After=scurebox.service systemd-logind.service systemd-user-sessions.service plymouth-quit-wait.service}}, {{Wants=scurebox.service}}, {{Conflicts=getty@tty1.service}}, {{StartLimitIntervalSec=0}}.
** {{User}} and {{Group}} = the kiosk user, {{PAMName=login}}, {{TTYPath=/dev/tty1}}, {{TTYReset}}, {{TTYVHangup}}, {{TTYVTDisallocate=yes}}, {{StandardInput=tty-fail}}, {{UtmpIdentifier=tty1}}, {{UtmpMode=user}}.
** Environment: {{XDG_SEAT=seat0}}, {{XDG_VTNR=1}}, {{XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland}}, {{XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/<uid>}}, {{WLR_NO_HARDWARE_CURSORS=1}}, {{XCURSOR_SIZE=1}}, {{HOME=<home>}}.
** {{ExecStartPre}}: {{-plymouth deactivate}}; {{+-/usr/bin/chvt 1}}; remove {{/run/user/<uid>/wayland-*}} and {{<home>/.config/chromium/Singleton*}}.
** {{ExecStart=/usr/bin/labwc -C /etc/scurebox/labwc -s /opt/scurebox/deploy/kiosk/scurebox-kiosk.sh}}, {{ExecStartPost=-/bin/sh -c 'sleep 6; /usr/bin/plymouth quit'}}.
** {{Restart=always}}, {{RestartSec=2}}, {{KillMode=control-group}}, {{TimeoutStopSec=8}}, {{WantedBy=graphical.target}}.
* {{scurebox-kiosk.sh}}:
** Browser: {{chromium}}, else {{chromium-browser}}.
** Run {{wlr-randr --output DSI-1 --on}} when the tool exists.
** Loop forever: start the browser with {{--kiosk --noerrdialogs --disable-infobars --no-first-run --disable-session-crashed-bubble --disable-pinch --overscroll-history-navigation=0 --disable-features=Translate,TranslateUI --disable-translate --lang=en-US --touch-events=enabled --enable-features=OverlayScrollbar --password-store=basic --check-for-update-interval=31536000 --disable-component-update --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required --ozone-platform=wayland --default-background-color=0e1418ff --hide-scrollbars --start-maximized --app=file:///opt/scurebox/deploy/kiosk/loading.html}}, then {{sleep 2}}.
* {{chromium-policy.json}}:
** {{URLBlocklist ["*"]}}, {{URLAllowlist ["localhost:3001","127.0.0.1:3001","file://*"]}}
** {{DeveloperToolsAvailability 2}}, {{PrintingEnabled false}}, {{DownloadRestrictions 3}}, {{AllowFileSelectionDialogs false}}, {{ExtensionInstallBlocklist ["*"]}}, {{BrowserSignin 0}}
** {{RestoreOnStartup 4}}, {{RestoreOnStartupURLs ["http://localhost:3001"]}}
** {{TranslateEnabled false}}, {{PasswordManagerEnabled false}}, {{DefaultNotificationsSetting 2}}
* {{labwc/rc.xml}}: decoration none, gap 0, adaptiveSync no, cornerRadius 0. Empty keybinds neutralise A-Tab, A-F4, W-Return, A-Escape and C-A-BackSpace. A windowRule for {{*}} toggles decorations off and maximizes. Touch naturalScroll is no.
* {{loading.html}}:
** Background {{#0e1418}}, text {{#e6ebf0}}, {{cursor:none}}.
** {{logo.png}} at 32vh, an animated bar 22vw wide and 4px high, a message line in {{#8f9aa5}}.
** Script: poll {{GET http://localhost:3001/api/state}} ({{cache:no-store}}) once a second. On {{r.ok}}, run {{location.replace("http://localhost:3001/")}}. After more than 180 tries, show "Service required - the application did not start" and keep polling.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# The compositor and browser restart forever: {{StartLimitIntervalSec=0}} plus the shell loop.
# Stale Wayland sockets and Chromium Singleton locks are removed before each start.
# Stopping must never hang: the whole cgroup is killed after 8 s.
*Configuration:* the kiosk user (uid 1000) is rendered by {{install.sh}}.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* After boot in browser mode the loading page appears, then the React UI.
* Navigating to another host is blocked.
* Alt+F4 and Alt+Tab do nothing.
* Killing chromium brings it back within about 2 s.
*Tests:* manual on the unit.
*Reference (source):* {{deploy/kiosk/*}}

---

column4: OPS-11 Vendored React web UI (ui/dist, served as wwwroot)
column5:
h3. Links
*Features:* Kiosk web UI, API host & infrastructure
*Blocked by:* OPS-01, API-04, API-01
*Blocks:* OPS-10
*Relates to:* API-05, API-06, API-08, API-10, API-11
*Implements:* OD-61, OD-63, OD-73, OD-42, REQ-25

*Project / folder:* {{ui/dist/}} (build output of the separate sCure-A React project), served by {{src/SCureBox.Api}}
*Goal:* Ship the existing React kiosk UI (Step A) unchanged, as a vendored build artifact. The API host serves it at {{/}} with an SPA fallback. The React UI drives the machine through the same {{/api}} contract as the native UI and the QA tools.
*Depends on:* OPS-01. Api (StaticUi mapping, CORS open, port 3001), Kiosk-Web (if that area rebuilds the React source).
*Files to create:* copy {{ui/dist/}} as built. Do not hand-edit it. The 15 files:
* {{index.html}}
* {{assets/index-<hash>.js}}, {{assets/index-<hash>.css}}
* {{assets/geist-{cyrillic,latin,latin-ext}-wght-normal-<hash>.woff2}}
* {{favicon.svg}}, {{icons.svg}}
* {{config/errors.json}}, {{config/system.json}}, {{config/versions.json}}
* {{materials/st45.csv}}
* {{videos/usb-insert.mp4}}, {{videos/usb-org.mp4}}
* {{compliance/sbom.json}} (CycloneDX 1.5, component {{scure-a-temp}} 0.0.0)
Total about 1.9 MB.
*Public contract:*
* How it is produced: {{npm run build}} (Vite) in the sibling {{sCure-A}} repo, then its {{dist/}} is copied to {{ui/dist}}. The build is sCure-A web version 0.9.4 ({{ui/dist/config/versions.json}} history[0] = 0.9.4, 2026-09-15). {{VITE_HW_API_URL}} is set at build time to {{http://localhost:3001/api}}. Asset paths are absolute ({{/assets/...}}), so the UI must be served from the domain root.
* {{index.html}}: {{lang="en"}} (must stay "en", or Chromium offers to translate from Hebrew), {{dir="ltr"}}, {{translate="no"}}, {{<meta name="google" content="notranslate">}}, viewport {{user-scalable=no}}, title {{sCure}}, {{<div id="root">}}.
* Packaging: {{SCureBox.Api.csproj}} copies {{../../ui/dist/**}} to {{wwwroot/}} (only when {{ui/dist/index.html}} exists). At runtime {{SCURE_UI_DIR}} (default {{<app>/wwwroot}}) is served with {{UseStaticFiles(ServeUnknownFileTypes=true)}}. The fallback returns {{index.html}} for any non-{{/api}} path. An unknown {{/api/*}} path returns {{404 {ok:false,message:"Not found"}}}. When there is no build, any non-API path returns {{404 {ok:false,message:"UI not built"}}}. {{/config/*.json}} is served from the UI dir, so the React UI reads its own errors.json, system.json and versions.json, not the firmware's {{config/}}.
* Client routes: {{/}}, {{/alerts}}, {{/cure-history}}, {{/cure-process}}, {{/material-editor}}, {{/network}}, {{/settings}}, {{/dev}}, {{/dev/led-calibration}}, {{/dev/hdt-calibration}}.
* Endpoints the bundle calls. The base is {{http://localhost:3001/api}}; materials, print-history and cure-history use a hard-coded {{http://localhost:3001}}.
** State and system: {{GET /api/state}} (1 s poll, 3 s timeout), {{GET /api/system/version}}, {{POST /api/system/datetime}}, {{/api/system/export-csv}}, {{/api/system/export-report}}, {{/api/system/export-logs}}, {{/api/system/reboot}}, {{GET /api/system/update/manifest}}, {{GET /api/system/update/package}}, {{POST /api/system/update}}.
** Cure: {{POST /api/cure/heat?target=}}, {{/cure/dry?target=}}, {{/cure/cure-405?target=&intensity=}}, {{/cure/cure-450?target=&intensity=}}, {{/cure/uv-only?wavelength=&intensity=&vent=}}, {{/cure/cool?target=&mode=}}, {{/cure/nitrogen?on=}}, {{/cure/stop[?immediate=1]}}.
** Chamber and outputs: {{/chamber/temperature?target=}}, {{/chamber/stop}}, {{/door/open}}, {{/door-abort/ack}}, {{/damper/open|close}}, {{/fans/<group>?speed=}}.
** Data: {{GET /api/materials/presets}}, {{GET/POST /api/materials/user}}, {{GET/POST /api/print-history}}, {{GET /api/cure-history}}, {{POST /api/cure-runs/<id>/start|telemetry|phase|finish}}, {{/api/cure-runs/<id>/report}}.
** Developer: {{/api/dev/log}}, {{/api/dev/led-calibration}} (+ {{/reset}}), {{/api/dev/led-power}}, {{/api/dev/picolog/status}}, {{/api/dev/hdt/status|start|abort|reset}}, {{/api/dev/hdt/report.csv}}.
** Also network and alerts pages ({{/api/network/*}}). See docs/03: "pre-flight = diagnostics/fan-test?fan=all (+ fans/override)".
* Polling only, no SSE or WebSocket: state 1 s, telemetry 5 s, alert summary 30 s, network status 3 s on the network page, HDT status 1 s. The UI is a fixed 800x480 canvas scaled to the window.
*Behaviour & rules:*
# Treat {{ui/dist}} as a binary drop. To update it, rebuild sCure-A and replace the whole folder.
# The API must listen on 3001 and keep CORS open, because the bundle hard-codes the absolute origin.
# The program sequencing state machine of the React UI is in the bundle (it calls one endpoint per phase). The firmware additionally offers {{/api/recipe/*}} (Application-Process).
*Configuration:* {{SCURE_UI_DIR}}.
*Acceptance criteria:*
* {{GET /}} returns text/html with {{<div id="root"}}.
* {{GET /settings}} and {{GET /cure/process/123}} return the same index body.
* {{GET /config/errors.json}} is JSON with at least 46 records, each with the keys code, key, severity, category, layer, message, description, troubleshooting, supportUrl, and code 7001 present.
* {{GET /api/no-such-route}} returns 404 {{{ok:false,"Not found"}}}.
*Tests:* {{tests/SCureBox.Api.Tests/StaticUiTests.cs}} (skips when ui/dist is missing); QA category {{static}}.
*Reference (source):* {{ui/dist/**}}, {{src/SCureBox.Api/SCureBox.Api.csproj}}, {{src/SCureBox.Api/Endpoints/StaticUi.cs}}, {{src/SCureBox.Api/Infrastructure/HostSettings.cs}}, {{docs/03-ui-and-qa.md}}

column4: OPS-12 OS image builder and CM5 eMMC flashing
column5: h3. Links *Features:* Deploy & OS image, Network & NetBird *Blocked by:* OPS-03, OPS-04, OPS-08, OPS-09 *Blocks:* OPS-13 *Relates to:* PLAT-05 *Implements:* OD-75, OD-76, EP-10, REQ-21 *Project / folder:* {{deploy/image/}} ({{build-image.py}}, {{flash-cm5.ps1}}, {{unxz.py}}, {{README.md}}), {{deploy/prepare-cm5.ps1}}, {{deploy/install-desktop-shortcut.ps1}} *Goal:* On a Windows PC, without WSL, Docker or admin rights for the build step, turn an official Raspberry Pi OS arm64 image into a ready-to-flash sCureBox image. Only the FAT boot partition is edited, and a first-boot script installs everything. The image is then written to the CM5 eMMC over rpiboot. *Depends on:* OPS-03 (payload), OPS-04, OPS-08, OPS-09. *Files to create:* the files listed above. *Public contract:* * {{python deploy/image/build-image.py}}. Options: ** {{--payload }} (default: newest {{deploy/out/scurebox-*-linux-arm64.tar.gz}}) ** {{--base-url}} (default {{https://downloads.raspberrypi.com/raspios_arm64_latest}}) or {{--base-image <.img|.img.xz>}} ** {{--user}} (default {{scure}}), {{--password}} (OPEN QUESTION / secret: the original uses a fixed well-known default; make it a required or configurable value), {{--hostname scurebox}}, {{--timezone Asia/Jerusalem}}, {{--no-ssh}} ** {{--out}}, {{--compress}} (also writes {{.img.xz}}, preset 6), {{--cache deploy/image/cache}} ** one of {{--netbird-setup-key}} / {{--netbird-setup-key-file}} ** Output: {{deploy/image/out/scurebox--cm5.img}}. The version is token [1] of the payload name. Requires {{pip install pyfatfs "setuptools<81" passlib}}. * {{flash-cm5.ps1 -Image [-DiskNumber N] [-ResumeFrom bytes] [-Yes] [-Elevated]}}. * {{prepare-cm5.ps1 [-BaseImage] [-Payload] [-User scure] [-Password …] [-Hostname scurebox] [-Timezone Asia/Jerusalem] [-DiskNumber] [-SkipTests] [-PrepareOnly] [-Yes] [-NoSsh] [-NetbirdSetupKeyFile] [-Help]}} runs publish.ps1, then build-image.py, then flash-cm5.ps1. * {{install-desktop-shortcut.ps1 [-Name "sCureBox CM5 Installer"]}} creates a desktop .lnk to {{powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File deploy\prepare-cm5.ps1}} and creates {{deploy\image\input}}. * {{unxz.py }} decompresses a file unchanged (8 MiB chunks). *Behaviour & rules:* # Download: resolve the redirect with a HEAD request. Download into the cache, reusing a cached file ({{.part}}, then rename, with a progress line). Verify against {{.sha256}}; skip the check if that file is unavailable; stop on a mismatch. Decompress with lzma. # The boot partition is the first MBR entry of type 0x0B, 0x0C or 0x0E; anything else stops the build ("not an MBR image" / "no FAT partition"). Stop when the payload plus 32 MiB is larger than the partition. # {{config.txt}}: append {{config-txt-fragment.txt}} and {{display-10inch.txt}} (CRLF normalised) when the first line of each is not already present. Replace {{\ndtparam=spi=on}} with {{\n#dtparam=spi=on}}. # {{cmdline.txt}}: remove {{ splash}} and {{ quiet}}, then append {{ quiet loglevel=0 vt.global_cursor_default=0}}. If {{systemd.run=}} is absent, also append {{ systemd.run=/boot/firstrun.sh systemd.run_success_action=reboot systemd.unit=kernel-command-line.target}}. # Write {{firstrun.sh}} (template placeholders {{@USER@ @HASH@ @HOSTNAME@ @TIMEZONE@ @SSH@}}) and {{scurebox-payload.tar.gz}}. Write {{userconf.txt}} as {{user:}}; Trixie needs it, or it boots into the first-user wizard. Write an empty {{ssh}} file unless {{--no-ssh}}. Write {{netbird-setup-key}} when a key is given; its format is validated like OPS-08. The password hash is passlib {{sha512_crypt}} with 5000 rounds, falling back to {{openssl passwd -6}}. Existing files are removed and written again (pyfatfs limitation). # {{firstrun.sh}} (logs to {{/var/log/scurebox-firstrun.log}}, {{set +e}}): ** Create the user: {{/usr/lib/userconf-pi/userconf USER HASH}}, or {{useradd -m -u 1000}} and add the user to adm, dialout, cdrom, audio, video, plugdev, games, users, input, render, netdev, gpio, i2c, spi, sudo. ** Hostname, ssh, keymap {{us}} and timezone through {{imager_custom}}, or a manual fallback. ** Extract the payload to {{/opt/scurebox-stage}}, chmod the scripts, run {{bash /deploy/install.sh --no-reboot --payload }}, then remove the stage and the payload. ** Remove {{firstrun.sh}} and strip {{ systemd.run.*}} from cmdline.txt. The systemd.run success action reboots. First boot takes about 2 to 3 minutes. # {{flash-cm5.ps1}}: ** Re-launch itself elevated through UAC when needed. The elevated run logs to {{%TEMP%\flash-cm5.log}} and the parent relays that log live. ** When no gadget disk is present (USB bus, friendly name matching {{mmcblk|nvme0n1|RPi|Raspberry}}), look for the boot-ROM device {{USB\VID_0A5C&PID_2712}} (CM5) or {{2711}} (CM4). Run {{C:\Program Files (x86)\Raspberry Pi\rpiboot.exe -d mass-storage-gadget64}} and wait up to 60 s for the disk. ** Exactly one candidate disk is required, unless {{-DiskNumber}} is given. The disk must be USB. The image must not be larger than the disk. Ask for the typed word {{FLASH}} unless {{-Yes}}. ** {{diskpart clean}}. Raw write to {{\\.\PhysicalDrive}} in 4 MiB chunks with WriteThrough, padded to 512 bytes. The first 4 MiB (the partition table) are written LAST, so Windows does not mount the boot partition during the write. ** Up to 12 retries on transient errors, re-running rpiboot when the disk vanished. Progress lines {{" NN% X MB Y MB/s"}} every 5 %. ** Verify by SHA-256 of the first 64 MiB. Print "flash complete … Power-cycle the CM5 (remove the nRPIBOOT jumper)". *Configuration:* user, password, hostname, timezone, SSH on/off, NetBird key file. *Acceptance criteria:* * The output {{.img}} boots on a CM5. The first boot creates the user and installs sCure, the unit reboots, and the native UI shows the Setup screen. * {{/var/log/scurebox-firstrun.log}} ends with "firstrun done". * No {{netbird-setup-key}} remains on the boot partition after enrollment. * The flasher refuses a non-USB disk and refuses when 0 or 2 or more candidates are found. *Tests:* manual (flash a unit). patch-display has unit tests (OPS-09). *Reference (source):* {{deploy/image/build-image.py}}, {{deploy/image/flash-cm5.ps1}}, {{deploy/image/unxz.py}}, {{deploy/image/README.md}}, {{deploy/prepare-cm5.ps1}}, {{deploy/install-desktop-shortcut.ps1}} ---

column4: OPS-12.1 Write build-image.py download/cache/verify/decompress of the Raspberry Pi OS arm64 base image
column5: HEAD-resolve the redirect, cached .part download with progress, verify against <url>.sha256 (skip if unavailable, stop on mismatch), lzma decompress; or use --base-image.

column4: OPS-12.2 Edit the FAT boot partition: config.txt, cmdline.txt firstrun, userconf.txt, ssh, NetBird key and payload
column5: Boot partition = first MBR entry 0x0B/0x0C/0x0E; stop when payload + 32 MiB exceeds it. sha512_crypt (5000 rounds, openssl fallback) userconf.txt; key format validated as OPS-08; output deploy/image/out/scurebox-<v>-cm5.img (+ .xz with --compress).

column4: OPS-12.3 Write the firstrun.sh template: user, hostname/ssh/keymap/timezone, extract payload and run install.sh --no-reboot
column5: Log to /var/log/scurebox-firstrun.log ending with firstrun done; remove firstrun.sh and the systemd.run tokens from cmdline.txt; systemd.run success action reboots.

column4: OPS-12.4 Write flash-cm5.ps1: UAC relaunch, rpiboot gadget, single USB disk check, raw write with partition table last, verify
column5: Look for 0A5C:2712/2711 and run rpiboot mass-storage-gadget64 (wait 60 s), refuse non-USB or 0 / 2+ candidates, typed FLASH unless -Yes, 4 MiB WriteThrough chunks, 12 retries, SHA-256 of first 64 MiB.

column4: OPS-12.5 Write prepare-cm5.ps1, install-desktop-shortcut.ps1 and unxz.py
